findings.title: Same NPE pattern left unfixed in sibling getSubGroupsStream overloads
findings.body: getSubGroupsCount() was fixed to null-check the result of modelSupplier.get() before calling getSubGroupsCount() on it, to avoid the NPE reported in #40368. However, the three overloaded getSubGroupsStream(...) methods just below it (lines ~255-268) use the exact same pattern: `return modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...)` without checking whether modelSupplier.get() returned null. Since modelSupplier resolves the underlying GroupModel via cacheSession.getGroupDelegate().getGroupById(...), it can legitimately return null if the group was concurrently deleted — the very race this PR claims to fix. These methods will still throw an NPE under the same concurrent-deletion scenario, so the fix is incomplete.

findings.title: getSubGroupsCount() can now silently return null
findings.body: The fix changes getSubGroupsCount() to return null when the backing GroupModel can't be resolved (e.g. group deleted concurrently), instead of throwing an NPE. This is a behavior/contract change: previously the method either returned a count or threw; now callers that unconditionally unbox/use the Long result (e.g. GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount -> representation.setSubGroupCount(group.getSubGroupsCount())) may propagate a null count into the REST representation without it being documented as a possible value, or could NPE themselves if they ever assume a non-null Long. There's no test verifying the null-returning behavior itself or how downstream consumers are expected to treat it.

findings.title: Background thread in new test is never joined, causing a race in the assertion and a potential thread leak
findings.body: In createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti(), a background Thread is started to repeatedly call managedRealm.admin().groups().groups(...) while the main thread deletes groups. After setting deletedAll.set(true), the test immediately asserts caughtExceptions is empty without calling thread.join(). Because the background thread only checks deletedAll at the top of its loop, an exception thrown during the in-flight iteration (the one started just before the flag flip) may be added to caughtExceptions after the assertion already ran, making the test non-deterministically pass even when the bug it targets reproduces (false negative). Additionally, the thread is not joined or marked as a daemon, so it can keep running past the end of the test method, potentially interacting with a realm/session that is being torn down by other tests.
